title: residual-gradient-workbench: a browser workbench separating an OES-32 residual replay from a classical thermoelectric generator model
description:
residual-gradient-workbench is a dependency-free browser prototype with two strictly separate lanes. Lane 01 replays the normative OES-32 residual (r_i = |y_i - x_i|, R = max r_i) pinned to oes32-residual at b77b612, and applies one capped correction to the first worst component; a falling R is labelled a simulation and the work from the residual is always zero. Lane 02 is a classical linear Thevenin model of a thermoelectric generator (TEG) driven by explicit hot and cold reservoir temperatures.

Evidence. All default parameters are SYNTHETIC; no hardware experiment was performed. Model outputs are predictions, not measurements.

Limits. Predicted electrical output requires an external temperature gradient; zero or reversed gradients give no positive output. The Carnot fraction is a ceiling on heat-to-work conversion, not the device efficiency. The two lanes share no state or energy accounting. No free-energy claim.
notes: Evidence status: SYNTHETIC parameters only; no hardware experiment performed. Residual change contributes zero work. Commercial licensing: see COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md.
